claim: Voice Agents sidebar tree: Search; Home; Build (Agents, Workflows, Knowledge base); Deploy (Phone numbers, Inbound calls, Outbound campaigns, Deploy with code); Monitor (Agent analytics, Workflow Analytics, Boards, Call logs); footer (What's new [New], Settings, MCP [New], Usage, Pricing, Documentation). The Home/Build/Deploy sections and the Monitor group are never visible in one frame: the sidebar is a scroll container that clips at 720 px height (Inbound calls fades with a double chevron in 02; Outbound campaigns is half-clipped in 27; 22 shows the scrolled state).

The outer icon rail has six unlabelled product icons with the third (a pixel robot) highlighted for Voice Agents. The six products are inferred from the workspace row, which lists Code, Content Studio, Cowork, Doc Agents, Sarvam API and Voice Agents; the icon-to-product mapping is not labelled anywhere.

The agent builder has five left tabs (Instructions, Variables, Tools, Settings, Automated tests), a version selector reading 'v1 · Draft', and header actions 'Improve with Genie', 'Test agent' (black primary) and an overflow menu. 'Improve with Genie' disappears from the header while the Genie side panel or the Test Agent panel is open.

Home and Agents both lead with 'What should your voice agent do?', a one-line prompt box ('Create a voice agent') and Ask Genie. Agents adds a 'Create from scratch' button, filter chips (All, Collections, Reminder, Recovery, Lead qualification) and template cards (Appointment..., Sales discovery 'Meet Ananya', EMI Collection). Home adds a Recents table (agent, owner, relative last-edited). Neither page shows an agent list above the fold on Agents.

The only first-run element captured is a product-announcement modal, 'Meet Bulbul V4 Voices' (Know more / Not now / X), shown over the Agents page on an account created 26 Aug 2026. It is a what's-new splash, not a setup checklist; no onboarding wizard, role or volume question was captured (the account pre-dates the evaluation).

The modal says Bulbul V4 is 'up to 40% faster than Bulbul V3', 'more expressive, with better emphasis and pacing' and speaks 'names and numbers more accurately'. Only the 40% is numeric; none of it is measured by us and the baseline is not stated.

The modal's cropped preview shows Sarvam's own template prompt: a greeting with variable chips ('Hi [userName], this is Aarti from [serviceProviderName]. Is this a good time to talk?'), then Persona, Environment & Situation, Objective and Speaking Style sections. Legible fragments include 'If asked whether you are AI: say you are a virtual assistant from the...' and 'Under 25 words per turn; one question at a time; wait for respo...'. Text is tiny and clipped; it was read from the pixels by us.
A new agent's greeting defaults to 'Hi, I am Shubh calling from Sarvam, how can I help you today?': it names the default voice and the vendor, with a per-greeting Translations button.

The Instructions editor is empty by default with the placeholder 'Write the agent prompt. Type / for commands, @ to mention variables or tools.', a floating 'Review agent' pill, and a Genie side panel ('What's on your mind?' with three suggestions: inbound support agent, add a knowledge base, get an agent ready to take live calls). Greeting and Instructions labels carry dotted underlines (tooltips, unopened).

The builder has no visible save, publish or commit control and no unsaved-changes indicator on any captured tab; the only state shown is the version label 'v1 · Draft'. The version dropdown and overflow menu were never opened, so version history, diff and the commit action's location in the builder are unknown. The commit requirement surfaces only later, in the campaign modal.

Variables tab: Input variables (columns Variable name, Default value; one row user_name = 'Manan') and Output variables (Variable name, Data type, Extraction prompt; one row call_summary, string, 'A short 1-2 line description of what happened on the call'). A 'When does a call count as a win?' card with 'Set call goal' appears only on the Output sub-tab, with no goal set. Whether user_name and call_summary are platform defaults or evaluator-created is not shown; the Test Agent Setup row reads '{ } 1/1'.

System tools tab lists five built-in tools, all 'During call' and 'Built-in': End Interaction (on), Query Knowledge Base (Off: 'Enable a knowledge base to turn on this tool'), Call Transfer (Off: 'Enable Call forwarding to turn on this tool'), Handle Voicemail (on), Change Output Language (on). Disabled state is shown by grey text, an 'Off' tag and a prerequisite hint, with no toggle on the row.

'Add a tool' offers four custom tool types, none badged Beta or Enterprise: API Tool, Data Validator (format and validity, e.g. email or phone number), Data Verifier (match against a value on file, e.g. last 4 digits of a phone number) and Mock API (test tool calls before your API exists). Selection is by clicking a card; there is no footer button.

The API Tool opens a right slide-over with a numbered stepper: 1 Name & describe (tool name in snake_case, required 'What does this tool do?' with a greyed 'Improve', run timing radio: when the call starts / during the conversation [pre-selected] / when the call ends); 2 Set up the API call (method select, URL, 'Send' to test, tabs Path, Params, Headers, Auth, Body, 'Paste a cURL to auto-fill'); 3 Send fields from the API response to the agent (text area with '@' field insertion). 'Add tool' is black from the start; no validation state is visible.

No DTMF, SMS, hang-up-with-reason, MCP, calendar or CRM tool appears in the five system tools or the four custom tool types. Bounded negative over the captured Tools surfaces only (the Custom tools tab itself was not captured); it agrees with the earlier docs finding that DTMF is 'planned'.

Speaking defaults on a new agent: Voice 'Shubh'; Per-language voices OFF (badge 'Overrides default voice'); Speaking speed 1.15 x; Pitch 0.00; Volume 1.0; Pronunciation dictionary upload (badge 'Advanced'). Sliders pair with a typed number field; none shows min or max ends. Model temperature is a 5-tick slider with its thumb at the middle tick labelled 'Balanced' and no number.

The mapping from the 'Balanced' temperature position to a number is unknown. The earlier docs finding was a range 0.1-0.9 with default 0.3; a mid-track thumb on a 5-tick scale would be 0.5 if linear, so the dashboard default may differ from the documented default, or the scale is not linear.

No LLM picker and no ASR (transcriber) picker appears in the captured Settings; the Thinking & knowledge section shows only Model temperature at its top, and the evaluator's notes say 'no LLM model picker seen - temperature only'. Rows below temperature on the Settings tab (knowledge base attach) were not captured, so this is a bounded negative.

The voice catalogue capture (a virtualised picker with 'Loading more') holds 199 distinct voice names: 176 role-named (e.g. 'Ritu - Hindi Support Agent') and 23 plain names (e.g. 'Shubh', 'Aayan') that carry a generic 'warm and natural tone' description and sit under a 'Bulbul v3' marker. Instinct reported about 222 voices; our count of 199 names is a lower bound because the dump keeps only unique lines.

Of the 196 catalogue entries with a parseable description, 119 are female and 77 male. 'Best for' job tags: natural back-and-forth conversation 30, customer support 18, long-form narration 13, e-learning 8, collections and payment recovery 8, outbound sales and lead qualification 7, banking and BFSI support 6, with single-digit counts for insurance, healthcare, e-commerce, KYC, feedback survey and interview screening. Category chips include Companion, Educational, Social Media, Advertisement, Assistant & IVR and News & Sports; names include 'AI Companion', 'Warm Night Companion' and 'Therapist Voice'. Computed by us from the text capture.

Language coverage inside the voice catalogue is uneven: Hindi 83 voices, English 43, English+Hindi 11, Marathi 9, Kannada 4, Punjabi 4, Telugu 4, Tamil 3, Gujarati 3, Bengali 2, Assamese 2, Western English 2, and three Hindi+regional mixes (Kannada, Malayalam, Telugu). Odia is a filter option but has no Odia voice in the capture; Malayalam has only a Hindi+Malayalam mix narrator. Assamese has 2 voices ('Great for Assamese') but Assamese is not among the 11 filter and agent languages. 'Hinglish' appears only inside 3 voice names, never as a language option.

The picker has filters Genders, Models (Bulbul v4 / v3) and 11 language chips (Hindi, Bengali, English, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu), a per-language 'Great for X' tag, a preview text box with a '135 / 500' character counter, and Cancel / 'Use Shubh' buttons. The evaluator reports natural-language search (e.g. 'hindi collections'); that search box is not in the text capture.

The default voice chip reads plain 'Shubh', which matches a plain-name (v3-style) catalogue entry, while the changelog says the V4 voice was renamed 'Shubh - Hinglish Ad Voice'. That suggests a new agent can default to a Bulbul V3 voice that reaches end of life on 2026-11-10. Alternative: the chip shows a short alias of the V4 voice. The model behind the chip was not opened.

The What's new modal states Bulbul V3 reaches end of life on Voice Agents on November 10, 2026 and tells users to switch every V3 agent to V4 before then. The entry has the same visual style as feature news, with no warning colour or badge.

Latency, cost and quality trade-offs are not shown where choices are made: the voice picker text, the Settings rows and the Test Agent panel carry no per-voice or per-model latency or price, and the Voice Agent minute is one bundled rate. The only latency figure in the product is the aggregate 'Latency' KPI in Agent Analytics (0 ms when empty) and the unquantified-baseline '40% faster' modal claim. Compare Vapi and ElevenLabs, which show inline latency and cost per model.

Language personalisation rows: Switch language during call (ON), Languages allowed (multi-select; chips Hindi, Bengali, '+9' = 11 selected by default; Hindi greyed and locked as 'Starting language'; options carry native-script glyphs), Auto-detected language switch, Switch after, Starting language (values hidden behind the open dropdown), Output numbers in Indic (appears ON; helper '500' -> 'paanch sau'). The Test Agent Setup row shows Hindi.

Idle-nudge default: 'Hey, are you still on the call?' after 5 seconds, with a drag handle, per-message translate icon, 'Add More' (several nudges) and 'Regenerate Translations'. 'Hang up after unanswered nudges' is ON by default ('End the call if the caller still doesn't respond'); how many unanswered nudges trigger the hang-up is not visible.

Voicemail appears in two places: the 'Handle Voicemail' system tool ('Detect if the call has reached a voicemail system...') and a Settings toggle 'Voicemail' (ON; 'Leave a message when voicemail is detected') with an editable message defaulting to 'Hey, seems like I have reached your voicemail. I shall call you back at a later time'. The default message names no company and no purpose. How the tool and the setting relate is not explained on screen.
Max call length defaults to 15 with a stepper control; helper text 'Ends the call after this many minutes (up to 60)'. The unit (minutes) is stated only in the helper text.

Call forwarding is OFF and greyed; helper: 'Transfer the caller to a human agent when the AI triggers a transfer. Only supported for Vobiz...' (truncated). The Call Transfer system tool stays Off until forwarding is enabled. Whether the toggle is disabled by the missing telephony connection or by provider limits is not shown.

Turn-taking numbers are not visible anywhere in the captured builder: the only time values are the nudge delay (seconds) and max call length (minutes). The Listening section (barge-in 'Let callers interrupt', eagerness to respond, volume threshold) is reported by the evaluator but has no screenshot, so its labels, levels and defaults are unverified. This is consistent with the earlier account-phase finding of three coarse controls over ten frame-level VAD parameters, and means a builder cannot see or sum a reply floor the way Bolna's 500 ms + 900 ms sliders expose one.

Environment section: Background sound defaults to 'Quiet office' (select with a play-preview button; helper 'Ambient noise behind the agent') and Background volume is a slider with no number, thumb about one third along. This adds ambience to the agent's audio; it is not caller-side noise suppression.

Whether a caller-noise denoiser, DTMF input handling or an echo setting exists is unknown: the region of Settings between Model temperature and Background sound (Listening, knowledge base) was not screenshotted.

The Test Agent panel docks beside the editor with a Voice / Phone / Chat switch. Voice shows 'Start a call to test the agent' and a black 'Start Call'; Phone shows 'Enter a number and place an outbound call', a 'Call to' field without a visible country-code control, and a grey disabled 'Place Call'. A Setup row summarises 'Hindi' and '{ } 1/1'. No latency, cost or model line is shown before a call. No call was started.

Automated tests tab is an empty state: 'Know if your agent works - Create test cases or let AI generate them - then run them and see exactly what passed, what failed, and why', with 'New test' and 'Read docs'. No AI-generate control is visible in the empty state and no test or result was captured. A simulated test run is priced at Rs 2 (see wt-sarvam-49).

Knowledge base page is a searchable table (Name, Uploaded by, Uploaded at 'Now') with 'Create knowledge base'. The one row has no status, size, source type or document count, so ingestion success is not visible. The create form and the agent-side attach control were not captured.

The Workflows page renders a completely blank main panel (no header, empty state, spinner or upsell). The evaluator's notes label it 'Enterprise-only, explicit upsell message [27]' but the PNG does not show that message, so the gating is not evidenced by the capture (earlier docs research said workflows are Enterprise-gated).

Phone numbers (no numbers connected) is a two-card chooser 'Take your agent live': 'Rent from Sarvam' (add or release anytime; billed through Sarvam Credits; 'Usage-based pricing · View details'; 'Powered by Vobiz'; Get started) versus 'Bring your own telephony' (works with 7 providers: Exotel, Smartflo, Pulse, InTalk, Vobiz, Twilio, Plivo; Connect). There is no numbers table or empty-list view.
The chooser claims 'Set up fully managed telephony infra in 2 minutes' and 'Integrate your existing telephony instantly'. Neither time was measured; no purchase or connection was made.

Outbound campaigns empty state: 'Reach thousands of customers by phone - Upload a contact list, pick an agent, and launch automated outbound calls', buttons 'Create campaign' (primary) and 'Build with API'. The 'Schedule campaign' modal has four stepper segments (Agent, Recipients, Schedule, Review & Launch) and 'Step 1 of 4'. Step 1 fields: Campaign name*, Select agent*, Version, Connections* (Connection select, Phone numbers select with 'By number / By group'). Phone numbers is disabled until a connection is chosen. In the empty form 'Next' looks enabled (black).

Selecting a draft version immediately shows 'This version is not committed - Switch to a committed version or commit this version before deploying' with a 'Commit version' button in the same step, and 'Next' turns grey. The screenshot cannot show whether Next is disabled by the draft, by the empty Connection, or both. The evaluator named the campaign 'DO NOT LAUNCH'; no campaign was created.

No consent, DND, DLT, calling-window or retry field appears on the campaigns empty state or on step 1. DND appears only as a card ('DND lists - Manage do not disturb lists') in the Deploy-with-code API recipes; no DND screen exists in the captured sidebar or pages. Bounded negative: steps 2-4 were not reached.

Not captured, so unknown from the dashboard: campaign steps 2-4 (recipient upload and validation, schedule window, retries, review), the KYC flow and price shown for renting a number (the evaluator's Rs 59 per number and 11/79/80 series come from notes and earlier docs, not from any screenshot), the Inbound calls page, and the BYO connection forms.

Agent Analytics (breadcrumb 'v2v / All Agents') has seven tabs (Overview, Connectivity, Engagement, Tools, Goals, Group by, Call Logs), an 'All Campaigns' chip, a date range (Oct 15-21, 2026), 'Add filter', a '#' / '%' toggle, a Day granularity select and six KPI tiles (Calls attempted, Connected call, Latency, Avg call duration [label truncated], Total minutes, Short calls) over 'Call outcomes' and 'Top failure reasons' cards. All values are zero. Empty-state quirks: Latency shows '0 ms' not a dash, and a decorative wavy line is drawn behind 'No data available'.

Call Logs is a tab inside Agent Analytics as well as a sidebar item; its default filter is 'Connected' (alternative 'All'), with column, download and overflow icon buttons and an empty state ('No call logs') whose primary action is 'Go to My Agents', not a way to place a test call. Table columns were not seen.

The analytics scope selector reads 'v2v', which is not the name of the only workspace in the Workspaces list (a workspace named for the account owner). What 'v2v' scopes (a product, project or app group) is not shown.

Billing shows a 'Pay as you go' badge, credits left -36.58 in the same dark type as a positive balance (no red, no overdrawn label), three cards (View plans, Add credits, Set up auto top-up), tabs Payment history ('No payments yet') and Billing details. The Plans page header pill and the Pricing page pill show '-37 Credits', so the balance is displayed with two roundings. Credits carry no currency symbol on Billing.

Plan cards as displayed: Pay As You Go (current; no monthly fee), Pro Rs 9,999 / month with 9,999 credits included ('Most popular'), Growth Rs 49,999 with 49,999 credits ('Best value'), Business Rs 1,99,999 with 1,99,999 credits. Tiers differ by qualitative text ('Lower rates', 'Higher rate limits', 'Our best public rates'); no numeric rate limit or per-minute rate is on the cards. A notice (top clipped) reads 'Complete your billing details so we can work out the tax. Nothing is charged until then.'

Per-service rate table as displayed (columns Pay As You Go / Pro / Growth / Business): Simulate Test Runs Rs 2 / 2 / 2 / 2 per run; Voice Agent (60s) Rs 3.5 / 3.25 / 3.15 / 3 per minute under 'Usage (Actual Minutes)'; Call forwarding to PSTN Rs 0.4 / 0.4 / 0.4 / 0.4 per 30s pulse. One bundled voice-agent rate; no STT, LLM or TTS breakdown. Further forwarding rows are clipped.

The dashboard resolves two prior conflicts: plan fees follow the docs (Rs 9,999 / 49,999 / about 2 lakh, with Business at Rs 1,99,999), not the marketing page's Rs 2,000 / 10,000 / 50,000; and Business is offered with a live 'Upgrade to Business' button at Rs 3 per minute, where the earlier docs reading said Business was 'coming soon'. Comparison of captured values against earlier claims.

Voice Agents Settings has two tabs, API Key and Secrets. With Secrets selected the panel is blank: no empty state, list, add button or spinner, so empty, loading and failed are indistinguishable. The API Key tab was not captured; no key was created. Org Policy, General, SSO, 2FA and audit-log screens were not captured.

'Deploy with code' offers API keys, Read docs, 'Set up for AI coding tool' (dropdown) and 'Generate API key', then six recipe cards: Instant outbound, Batch outbound calling, Inbound deployments, Data fetch, Agents SDK, DND lists. There is no 'create or edit an agent' recipe, which agrees with earlier findings that agent authoring is dashboard, Genie and MCP only. Cards show only an icon, title and one line; no code is shown.

The MCP page is a two-step setup: paste an mcp.json (server name sarvam-voice-agents, host mcp.sarvam.ai, path cut off after '/voice-agent') or press 'Add to Cursor' / 'Add to Claude', then verify by asking the client 'List my voice agents'. Clients named: Cursor, Claude, Windsurf, Sarvam Code and any MCP-aware client. The snippet shows no key or auth step.

Organisation Settings nav: General, Members, Workspaces, Policy; Billing & usage: Plans & pricing, Billing, Usage; Support, Terms of service, Privacy policy. 'Add User' takes only an email and a workspace and states 'Invite a user as a Member with Editor access'; there is no role selector. One workspace carries all six products; 'Add Workspace' exists.

The What's new modal lists five entries (newest first): Dual-Channel Call Recordings (stereo, user left, agent right; 5 days ago), Bulbul V3 End of Life (14 Oct), Volume Adjustment (slider in voice settings, 'from 0.7...'; 14 Oct), Bulbul V4 for Voice Agents with a filterable voice catalogue (6 Oct), New Voice Names in Bulbul V4 (6 Oct). Dates mix relative and absolute without a year; two summaries are truncated.

Genie, the AI copilot, is present on nearly every page: 'Ask Genie' top right (with a transient 'Hi' tooltip on some pages), a docked panel in the builder with build/edit/test suggestions and history, 'Improve with Genie' in the builder header and 'Review agent' in the editor. The agent-creation prompt box on Home and Agents is a second AI entry point. What Genie actually builds was not exercised.
